mainTopic: Canopies and hats as אהל on שבת; רב's three teachings; will the תורה be forgotten?
overview: The גמרא opens by allowing a sloped bridegroom's canopy (כילת חתנים) to be set up and taken down on שבת. רב ששת בריה דרב אידי limits this with four conditions: nothing about the canopy may form a 'roof' of a טפח, since that would make it an אהל. He also permits wearing a brimmed felt hat (סיאנא). The גמרא first resolves a conflicting report by brim width, then rejects that answer and concludes that the hat is allowed only when it fits firmly, so it won't blow off and be carried. Next, רב הונא sends רמי בר יחזקאל three teachings of רב. Two are about שבת: spreading a wineskin is allowed only with two people (אביי adds that a canopy is forbidden even with ten), and a stove missing even one leg may not be moved. The third is that the תורה will one day be forgotten, which the Sages of יבנה also learn from עמוס. They picture a woman whose question about her תרומה loaf no one can answer, which the גמרא sharpens into a question of ראשון or שני לטומאה. Finally, רבי שמעון בן יוחי insists the תורה will never be forgotten and begins to reinterpret the פסוק in עמוס; his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A bridegroom's canopy may be set up and taken down on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The base ruling: a כילת חתנים may be spread out and dismantled on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bridegroom's canopy: it is permitted to spread it out, and it is permitted to take it down.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל, quoting רבי חייא (end of the previous amud), states a base rule: a groom's canopy, which slopes and has no flat roof, may be put up and taken down on שבת. The next steps will set limits on this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making an אהל (a tent-like covering) on שבת is normally forbidden. This canopy is allowed because it has no real flat roof. It is just sloping cloth draped over a bed.

keyTerms.meaning: a bridegroom's canopy draped over the bed
to spread it out / set it up
to dismantle it / take it down
a tent or roof-like covering; making one is forbidden on שבת

phrases.english: A bridegroom's canopy
phrases.notes: A sloped canopy with no flat roof

phrases.english: it is permitted to spread it
and it is permitted to dismantle it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening base teaching of this passage
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sloped כילת חתנים may be spread and taken down on שבת because it is not a real אהל.

steps.title: First limit: the canopy's top must be less than a handbreadth wide
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי says the היתר applies only when the canopy's top is narrower than a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי said: We only said this when its roof is not a handbreadth wide. But if its roof is a handbreadth wide, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts narrowing the rule from step 1. The canopy is permitted only if its top is less than a טפח wide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flat top of a טפח counts as a real roof. That would make the canopy an אהל, which may not be made on שבת. So the היתר only covers a canopy that comes to a narrow peak.

keyTerms.meaning: we only said this when… (formula that limits a rule)
a handbreadth, the minimum size for a roof

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, said:
We only said it
where its roof is not a handbreadth wide;
but if its roof is a handbreadth wide, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the base ruling of step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the canopy's top is a טפח wide, setting it up is forbidden.

steps.title: Second limit: no handbreadth width within three handbreadths of the top
steps.stepSummary: Even with a narrow top, the canopy is forbidden if it widens to a טפח within three טפחים below the top.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even when its roof is not a handbreadth wide, we only said it is permitted when there is no handbreadth of width within three handbreadths of its roof. But if there is a handbreadth of width within three handbreadths of its roof, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds a second condition. The canopy must not reach a טפח of width within three טפחים of its peak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that gaps of less than three טפחים are treated as closed. So width reached that close to the top counts as if it were the top itself. The top would then be treated as a roof of a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: the rule that gaps under three טפחים are treated as joined

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new kind of roof. It is the same 'roof of a טפח' test from step 2, measured with the rule that anything within three טפחים counts as touching.

phrases.english: And even when its roof is not a handbreadth wide,
we only said it is permitted
where there is not, within less than three
handbreadths near its roof, a handbreadth of width;
but if there is, within less than three
handbreadths near its roof, a handbreadth of width, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֵין בְּגַגָּהּ טֶפַח נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further limit on top of step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טפח of width within three טפחים of the top makes the canopy forbidden.

steps.title: Third limit: the slope itself must not have a handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: If the slope has a טפח, it is forbidden, because sloping tent walls count as tents.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said it is permitted when its slope does not have a handbreadth. But if its slope has a handbreadth, it is forbidden, because the slopes of tents are considered like tents.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds a third condition about the canopy's slope. He backs it with the principle שיפועי אהלים כאהלים דמו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think only a flat top counts as a roof. Here we learn that a slanted covering also counts as an אהל. So a slope of a טפח alone is enough to forbid the canopy.

keyTerms.meaning: the slopes of tents are treated like tents

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle שיפועי אהלים כאהלים is used in other areas of הלכה too, such as טומאת אהל.

phrases.english: And we only said it is permitted
where its slope does not have a handbreadth;
but if its slope has a handbreadth, it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: The word 'forbidden' isn't actually written here; the גמרא assumes it.

phrases.english: for the slopes of tents are considered like tents.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין בְּשִׁיפּוּעָהּ טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third limit in the same list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slope of a טפח makes the canopy an אהל, because slopes of tents count as tents.

steps.title: Fourth limit: the canopy must not hang a handbreadth below the bed
steps.stepSummary: If the canopy hangs a טפח below the bed frame, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we only said it is permitted when it does not hang down a handbreadth below the bed. But if it hangs down a handbreadth below the bed, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives the last condition: the canopy's cloth must not hang a טפח below the bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cloth drops a טפח below the bed, the bed itself acts as a roof. The hanging cloth then acts as a wall around the space under the bed. Together they form an אהל.
steps.whatToRemember: A כילת חתנים is permitted only if nothing gives it a 'roof' of a טפח. That rules out four things: a wide top, width near the top, a slope of a טפח, and cloth hanging a טפח below the bed.

phrases.english: And we only said it is permitted
where it does not descend a handbreadth below the bed;
but if it descends a handbreadth below the bed, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא נָחֵית מִפּוּרְיָא טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final limit in the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cloth hanging a טפח below the bed turns the bed into a roof, so it is forbidden.

steps.title: רב ששת permits wearing a brimmed felt hat
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי rules that wearing a סיאנא (felt hat) on שבת is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת בריה דרב אידי said: This felt hat is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling from the same אמורא: a brimmed felt hat may be worn on שבת. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wide brim sticks out over the head a bit like a small tent. Even so, רב ששת says the hat is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: a felt hat with a brim

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, said:
This felt hat is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling from the same אמורא on a related אהל topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wearing a סיאנא on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: Contradiction: another statement forbids the felt hat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a statement saying the סיאנא is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it stated: a felt hat is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's ruling with a different statement that forbids the same hat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two statements give opposite rulings about the same item. One of them seems wrong unless we can show they are talking about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: but wasn't it stated? (introduces a conflicting source)

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated: a felt hat is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's היתר for the סיאנא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A conflicting statement forbids the same hat.

steps.title: First answer: it depends on whether the brim is a handbreadth wide
steps.stepSummary: The ruling that forbids applies to a brim of a טפח. The ruling that permits applies to a smaller brim.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one, where the brim has a handbreadth, is forbidden. That one, where it does not have a handbreadth, is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases based on how wide the brim is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer treats the brim like the canopy: a brim of a טפח would be an אהל. So a wide brim is forbidden and a narrow one is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (introduces an answer)
this case… that case… (splits two sources into two situations)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where it has a handbreadth,
that one is where it does not have a handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two sources into two different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: A brim of a טפח is forbidden as an אהל; a smaller brim is permitted.

steps.title: Challenge: a cloak sticking out a handbreadth is not an אהל
steps.stepSummary: If a brim of a טפח were an אהל, then pulling a cloak out a טפח past the head would also make one liable, which is absurd.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, if one extended his cloak a handbreadth, would he also be liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 8. It shows that the answer leads to a ridiculous result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People often wear clothing that sticks out a טפח, and no one says they are making an אהל. So a brim of a טפח cannot be the real reason the hat is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so… (pushes a claim to an absurd result)

phrases.english: But if that is so,
if one extended his cloak a handbreadth,
would he also be liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a brim of a טפח is an אהל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By that logic a cloak sticking out a טפח would make one liable, which is absurd.

steps.title: Final answer: it depends on whether the hat sits firmly
steps.stepSummary: A firmly fitted hat is permitted. A loose hat is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult. This one is where it is fitted firmly; that one is where it is not fitted firmly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first answer and gives a new one. It splits the cases by whether the hat fits snugly on the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is no longer making an אהל. The worry is that wind may blow off a loose hat, and the person may then carry it four אמות in a public domain. A firmly fitted hat will not blow off, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (signals that the earlier answer is dropped)

steps.whatToRemember: The סיאנא is permitted when it sits tightly and forbidden when it is loose. The reason is the fear of carrying it if it blows off, not the laws of אהל.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the hat is forbidden because it makes an אהל. Step 9 rejected that idea. The final reason is the fear of carrying.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this one is where it is fitted firmly,
that one is where it is not fitted firmly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer from step 8, which step 9 rejected
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new way of splitting the cases, based on a different reason for the איסור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hat is forbidden because a brim of a טפח is an אהל.
steps.terutzMaskana: A loose hat is forbidden because it may blow off and be carried; a firm hat is permitted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The סיאנא is permitted when fitted firmly and forbidden when loose.

steps.title: רמי בר יחזקאל asks רב הונא for רב's three teachings
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל sends a request to רב הונא. He asks him to repeat three excellent teachings he once said in the name of רב: two about שבת and one about תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר יחזקאל sent a message to רב הונא: 'Please tell us again those excellent teachings you once told us in the name of רב, two about שבת and one about תורה.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is introducing a list of teachings from רב that will be explained in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet. רמי בר יחזקאל only names the outline: three teachings, two on שבת and one on תורה. The steps that follow will fill in each one.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to him (a message or letter)

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Yechezkel sent to Rav Huna:

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא לַן אִיזִי הָנָךְ מִילֵּי מְעַלְּיָיתָא
phrases.english: Please tell us those excellent teachings
that you told us in the name of Rav,
two about Shabbat and one about Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new unit of teachings from רב. The first of them continues the אהל theme from the canopy discussion in steps 1-5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What were the three teachings of רב (two about שבת, one about תורה) that רב הונא once reported?

steps.title: First שבת teaching: a large wineskin may be spread only by two people
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers with the first teaching. A ברייתא permits spreading a big wineskin by its straps on שבת. רב limits this: it is allowed only when two people do it together, not one person alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא sent back: About what a ברייתא teaches, 'It is permitted to spread a large wineskin by its straps on שבת,' רב said: They only taught this when two people do it together. One person alone is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the first of the שבת teachings. רב narrows a lenient ברייתא so that it applies only when two people spread the wineskin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sounds like a blanket permission. רב adds a limit. Two people can place the wineskin without pulling it tight. One person alone is likely to stretch it out like a tent, which would make an אהל.

keyTerms.meaning: Its straps or cords, used to hang it
To spread it out or stretch it
They only taught this in the case of... (a limiting formula)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to the אהל theme of the כילת חתנים in Steps 1-5. Spreading something tight above or around a space can count as making a tent on שבת.

phrases.english: He sent to him: Regarding that which was taught in a Baraita,
'It is permitted to spread a large wineskin by its straps on Shabbat':

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: Rav said: They only taught this when done by two people,
but by one person, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: One person would likely stretch it tight like a tent.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ: הָא דְּתַנְיָא גּוֹד בְּכִיסָנָא מוּתָּר לִנְטוֹתָהּ בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request in Step 11 with the first Shabbat teaching.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב limits the ברייתא's permission to spread a wineskin: two people may do it, one person may not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spreading a large wineskin by its straps on שבת is permitted only with two people. One person alone is forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: a canopy is forbidden even with ten people
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that spreading a כילה (canopy) is forbidden even if ten people do it together. It is impossible to avoid stretching it a little, which forms a tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And a canopy is forbidden even with ten people, because it is impossible that it will not get stretched a little.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי builds on רב's rule. He says that for a canopy, having more people does not help at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a wineskin, two people can avoid stretching it, so it is allowed. A canopy will always get pulled tight for at least a moment while it is being spread. That brief moment already makes an אהל, so the number of people does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: A canopy or tent-like drape (for example, over a bed)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the number of people is the real rule. What matters is whether the item gets stretched into a tent. The wineskin can avoid this. The canopy cannot.

phrases.english: Abaye said: And a canopy
is forbidden even with ten people.
It is impossible that it will not be stretched a little.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְכִילָּה אֲפִילּוּ בַּעֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter case beside רב's wineskin rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כילה may not be spread on שבת even by ten people, because it always gets stretched a little and becomes an אהל.

steps.title: Second שבת teaching: a stove whose leg fell off
steps.stepSummary: The second Shabbat teaching. A ברייתא says a stove that lost one leg may be moved, but one that lost two legs may not. רב forbids moving it even when only one leg fell, out of concern that a person will jam the leg back in.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the other teaching? As a ברייתא teaches: A stove that had one of its legs fall off may be moved. If two fell off, it is forbidden. רב said: Even if one fell off, it is also forbidden, as a decree in case a person firmly sticks the leg back in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the second Shabbat teaching was and answers with it. רב is stricter than the ברייתא about moving a stove with a missing leg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the ברייתא, a stove missing one leg is still a usable כלי, so it may be moved. With two legs missing it is a broken item and may not be moved. רב forbids even the one-leg case, because while handling it a person might push the leg firmly back in, which would be fixing a כלי on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest he fasten it (jam the leg firmly in)

steps.whatToRemember: רב's two שבת teachings: (1) a wineskin may be spread only by two people, and אביי adds that a כילה is forbidden even with ten; (2) a stove missing even one leg may not be moved, in case one jams the leg back in. The תורה teaching comes next.

phrases.english: The other one, what is it? As it was taught in a Baraita:
A stove that had one of its legs fall off,
it is permitted to move it.
If two fell off, it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ חַד נָמֵי אָסוּר,
phrases.english: Rav said: Even if one fell off, it is also forbidden,
as a decree lest he fasten it in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list from Step 11 and gives the second Shabbat teaching.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second teaching is רב's stringency on a stove: even with one leg missing it may not be moved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stove that lost even one leg may not be moved on שבת, as a גזירה lest one jam the leg back in and so fix a כלי.

steps.title: רב's teaching that the תורה will be forgotten
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא gives the third teaching of רב. The Torah is destined to be forgotten from ישראל. רב learns this by comparing the word 'הפלאה' in דברים with the same word in ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Torah: as רב said, the Torah is destined to be forgotten from ישראל. It says, 'And ה׳ will make your plagues astonishing.' I do not know what this 'astonishment' is. But another פסוק says, 'Therefore, I will continue to astonish this people with wondrous astonishment.' So you must say: this 'astonishment' is the forgetting of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא now gives the third and last teaching that רמי בר יחזקאל asked for, the one about תורה. רב says the Torah will one day be forgotten, and he proves it from פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curses in דברים speak of a strange 'הפלאה' (astonishment), and on its own that word is unclear. ישעיה uses the same word, and that פסוק continues with 'the wisdom of its wise will be lost.' So the 'astonishment' must mean that Torah wisdom will be lost.

keyTerms.meaning: Astonishment, a wondrous and strange punishment
You must say (the conclusion is forced)

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the list of three teachings that רמי בר יחזקאל asked for: two about שבת and one about תורה.

phrases.english: Torah — as Rav said:
phrases.notes: This is the third teaching, the one about Torah.

phrases.english: The Torah is destined to be forgotten from Israel,
as it says: 'And ה׳ will make your plagues astonishing,'
this 'astonishment' — I do not know what it is.
When it says: 'Therefore, behold, I will continue

phrases.aramaic: לְהַפְלִיא אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה הַפְלֵא וָפֶלֶא״
phrases.english: to astonish this people with wondrous astonishment'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 29:14. The פסוק goes on: 'the wisdom of its wise will be lost.'

phrases.english: you must say: this astonishment is Torah (being forgotten).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third teaching, after the two שבת teachings in steps 12 and 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רמי בר יחזקאל asked for the teaching about תורה (step 11).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah is destined to be forgotten, learned by linking 'הפלאה' in דברים to 'הפלאה' in ישעיה.

steps.title: The חכמים in יבנה teach the same idea from עמוס
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that the Sages gathered in the vineyard of יבנה. They said the Torah will be forgotten, and they proved it from two פסוקים in עמוס about a hunger for the word of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When our Sages entered the vineyard in יבנה, they said the Torah is destined to be forgotten from ישראל. It says, 'Days are coming, says ה׳, when I will send a hunger in the land. It will not be a hunger for bread or a thirst for water, but for hearing the words of ה׳.' And it says, 'They will wander from sea to sea and roam from north to east to seek the word of ה׳, but they will not find it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same message as רב: the Torah will be forgotten. The ברייתא learns it from different פסוקים, in ספר עמוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's teaching depended on a link between two words. The ברייתא uses פסוקים that say it openly: people will be 'hungry' for ה׳'s word and will search for it without finding it. This gives a second, independent source for the same idea.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'vineyard' in יבנה, the academy where the Sages sat in rows like vines

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
When our Sages entered the vineyard in Yavne, they said,
The Torah is destined to be forgotten from Israel,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הִנֵּה יָמִים בָּאִים נְאֻם ה׳ אֱלֹהִים
phrases.english: as it says: 'Behold, days are coming, says the Lord God,'
and I will send a hunger in the land,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָעָב לַלֶּחֶם וְלֹא צָמָא לַמַּיִם
phrases.english: not a hunger for bread and not a thirst for water,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִם לִשְׁמוֹעַ אֵת דִּבְרֵי ה׳״,
phrases.english: but for hearing the words of ה׳.'
And it is written: 'And they will drift from sea to sea,'
and from north to east they will roam

phrases.aramaic: לְבַקֵּשׁ אֶת דְּבַר ה׳ וְלֹא יִמְצָאוּ״.
phrases.english: to seek the word of ה׳, but they will not find it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ לַכֶּרֶם בְּיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel ברייתא with the same message as רב's teaching, using different פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Sages of יבנה said the Torah will be forgotten, based on the 'hunger for the word of ה׳' in עמוס.

steps.title: Three meanings of 'the word of ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that 'the word of ה׳' that people will not find means three things: הלכה, the time of the קץ (end of days), and נבואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The word of ה׳' means הלכה. 'The word of ה׳' means the end of days. 'The word of ה׳' means prophecy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains what 'the word of ה׳' in the פסוק means. It lists three things that will be lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is read three ways. People will search for clear הלכה, for knowledge of when the גאולה will come, and for נבואה, and they will not find any of them.

keyTerms.meaning: The end, the time of the final redemption

phrases.english: 'The word of ה׳' — this is halacha,
'The word of ה׳' — this is the end (of days),
'The word of ה׳' — this is prophecy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the key phrase in the פסוק quoted in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'The word of ה׳' that will be lost includes הלכה, knowledge of the קץ, and נבואה.

steps.title: What does 'roaming to seek the word of ה׳' look like
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what it means in practice that people will 'roam to seek the word of ה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'they will roam to seek the word of ה׳'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for a real-life picture of the wandering search in the פסוק, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is clear, but the גמרא wants a concrete example of what it will look like when people search for Torah and cannot find it.

phrases.english: And what is (the meaning of) 'they will roam to seek the word of ה׳'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a concrete picture of the פסוק quoted in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete picture of what the wandering search for ה׳'s word will look like.

steps.title: The woman with the תרומה loaf whom no one can answer
steps.stepSummary: A woman will take a loaf of תרומה and go from בית כנסת to בית מדרש asking whether it is טמא or טהור. No one will understand the question well enough to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: A woman will one day take a loaf of תרומה. She will go around to the בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות to find out whether it is טמא or טהור, and no one will understand.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a picture. A simple question about the purity of a תרומה loaf will go unanswered, because Torah knowledge will be lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'roaming' in the פסוק is the woman going from place to place. 'They will not find it' means even the places of Torah learning will not have someone who knows the הלכה. This shows the forgetting of Torah in a very practical way.

keyTerms.meaning: A loaf of תרומה, food given to כהנים that must stay pure
And there is no one who understands

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah teaching of רב: the Torah is destined to be forgotten. He learns it from 'הפלאה' in דברים and ישעיה. The Sages of יבנה learn it from the 'hunger for ה׳'s word' in עמוס, and picture it as a woman whose question about her תרומה loaf no one can answer.
steps.confusionAlert: Read at face value, this sounds as if even a basic purity question will go unanswered. The גמרא will challenge that reading in the next step, and step 21 explains that her real question is a technical one: whether the bread is a ראשון or a שני.

phrases.english: They said: A woman is destined
to take a loaf of teruma
and go around among the synagogues and study halls

phrases.aramaic: לֵידַע אִם טְמֵאָה הִיא וְאִם טְהוֹרָה הִיא,
phrases.english: to find out whether it is impure or whether it is pure,
and there will be no one who understands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: עֲתִידָה אִשָּׁה שֶׁתִּטּוֹל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 with a concrete example.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The woman going from place to place with her תרומה loaf, and no one able to rule on it, is the 'roaming without finding.'

steps.title: How can no one know if the loaf is pure or impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that whether food can become טמא is written openly in the Torah, so it cannot be the forgotten question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether it is pure or impure? That is written openly in the Torah: 'Of all the food that may be eaten.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from the previous step. It cannot be that no one will know whether a loaf can be טמא, because the Torah says it openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא says that food that touches טומאה becomes טמא. Even when the Torah is forgotten, a basic rule written plainly in a פסוק will still be known. So the woman's question must be about something harder.

phrases.english: Whether it is pure
or whether it is impure?
It is written openly about this:
'Of all the food that may be eaten' (Vayikra 11:34)!
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק teaches that such food becomes טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the case in step 19 can be described as unanswerable.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that no one will know whether the loaf is טמא or טהור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule stated openly in a פסוק cannot be the kind of knowledge that gets forgotten.

steps.title: The real question is the level of impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the woman wants to know whether the bread is a first or second degree of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: she wants to know whether it is a first degree or a second degree of impurity, and no one will understand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by making the question narrower. The woman already knows the bread is טמא. She is asking how strong its טומאה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new question is not 'pure or impure' but 'ראשון or שני לטומאה.' That is a more technical detail, so it is believable that it could be forgotten. The level matters because it decides how much טומאה the bread passes on to other things.

keyTerms.meaning: First degree of impurity, from touching a primary source
Second degree of impurity, from touching a ראשון

steps.confusionAlert: 'First' and 'second' here do not mean a first loaf and a second loaf. They are levels of טומאה: a ראשון is one step away from the source of טומאה, and a שני is two steps away.

phrases.english: Rather: to know whether it is first degree
or whether it is second degree,
and no one will understand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by reinterpreting the woman's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the question is narrowed to a more technical detail.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman was asking whether the bread is טמא at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: She knows it is טמא and is asking whether it is a ראשון or a שני.

steps.title: The level of impurity is also stated in a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a משנה already says that bread in an oven with a שרץ is a שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is a משנה! As we learned: if a שרץ is found in an oven, the bread inside is second degree, because the oven is first degree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 21. The exact level of the bread is taught openly in a משנה, so it would not be forgotten either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the משנה, the שרץ is the primary source of טומאה. It makes the oven a ראשון, and the oven makes the bread a שני. Since the answer is spelled out, the woman's question still seems easy to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead creeping creature, a primary source of טומאה
First degree of impurity (same as ראשון)

phrases.english: Is this not also a Mishnah?
As we learned:
A creeping creature that was found in the oven —
the bread inside it is second degree,
because the oven is first degree.
phrases.notes: The שרץ makes the oven a ראשון, and the oven makes the bread a שני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that no one will know whether the bread is a ראשון or a שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An open משנה already gives the answer (שני), so it would not be forgotten.

steps.title: People will be confused by רב אדא בר אהבה's suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that people will be unsure because of רב אדא בר אהבה's idea that the oven should be viewed as full of טומאה, which would make the bread a ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: They will be unsure about what רב אדא בר אהבה said to רבא: let us view this oven as if it were full of impurity, and the bread should be first degree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The confusion will come from a competing idea that seems to argue with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה suggested treating the whole inside of the oven as if the טומאה fills it. Then the bread would count as if it touched the שרץ itself, which would make it a ראשון, not a שני. In the future people will not know which view is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: As if it were filled with impurity

phrases.english: They will be in doubt

phrases.aramaic: הָא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: about what Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rava:
Let us view this oven
as if it were filled with impurity
and the bread should be first degree!
phrases.notes: The bread is treated as if it touched the שרץ directly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by pointing to a competing view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The open משנה is unclear in practice because a competing reasoning seems to oppose it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a משנה states the bread is a שני, no one could be in doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אדא בר אהבה's 'full of טומאה' idea will make people unsure whether the bread is a ראשון or a שני.

steps.title: רבא rejects the idea that the oven is full of impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that we do not view the oven as if it is filled with טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We do not say, 'Let us view this oven as if it were full of impurity.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב אדא בר אהבה's suggestion. In the next step he brings a source to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the oven is not treated as full of טומאה, then the bread did not 'touch' the שרץ. It only got its טומאה through the oven, so it stays a שני, just as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not say (we do not apply this reasoning)

phrases.english: He said to him: We do not say

phrases.aramaic: לֶיחְזְיֵיהּ לְהַאי תַּנּוּרָא כְּמַאן דִּמְלֵי טוּמְאָה.
phrases.english: 'Let us view this oven as if it were filled with impurity.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion quoted in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole 'full of טומאה' reasoning of רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The airspace of an earthenware vessel is not treated as if it were filled with the טומאה itself.

steps.title: Proof: vessels inside an earthenware vessel are not made impure by its airspace
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that only foods become טמא in the airspace of a כלי חרס, not vessels. This shows the airspace is not considered 'full of טומאה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: You might think all vessels become impure in the airspace of an earthenware vessel. So the Torah says, 'All that is in it shall be impure... of all the food that may be eaten.' Foods become impure in the airspace of an earthenware vessel, but vessels do not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his point from a ברייתא. Only food, not other vessels, becomes טמא from the inside air of a כלי חרס that has a שרץ in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the oven's airspace were truly 'full of טומאה,' anything inside, including vessels, would become טמא as if it touched the שרץ. Since vessels inside do not become טמא, the airspace is not treated that way. So food inside becomes טמא only through the oven, and it is a שני.

keyTerms.meaning: The inside airspace of an earthenware vessel

steps.confusionAlert: A כלי חרס does become טמא when a שרץ is in its airspace, and food inside it also becomes טמא. The ברייתא only says that other vessels inside it do not become טמא this way.
steps.whatToRemember: The woman's forgotten question is whether the bread is a ראשון or a שני. The משנה says it is a שני. רב אדא בר אהבה's 'oven full of טומאה' idea would make it a ראשון, but רבא rejects that idea from the ברייתא that vessels do not become טמא in the airspace of a כלי חרס.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a clear הלכה can still become confusing when a strong-sounding opposing argument exists. That is the kind of confusion the ברייתא predicts will come when תורה is forgotten.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יְהוּ כׇּל הַכֵּלִים מִיטַּמְּאִין
phrases.english: As it was taught: One might think all vessels become impure
in the airspace of an earthenware vessel,
therefore the verse says: 'All that is in it shall be impure' (Vayikra 11:33),
'of all the food that may be eaten' (Vayikra 11:34) —
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are next to each other, which teaches that 'all that is in it' means food.

phrases.english: foods become impure in the airspace of an earthenware vessel,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין כֵּלִים מִטַּמְּאִין בַּאֲוִיר כְּלִי חֶרֶס.
phrases.english: but vessels do not become impure in the airspace of an earthenware vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יְהוּ כׇּל הַכֵּלִים מִיטַּמְּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רבא's rejection in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the oven's airspace is not viewed as 'full of טומאה.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 11:33–34: only foods, not vessels, become טמא in the airspace of a כלי חרס.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: the תורה will never be forgotten
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון בן יוחי, who says it is unthinkable that the תורה would be forgotten from ישראל. He proves this from the פסוק "כי לא תשכח מפי זרעו".
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: Heaven forbid that the תורה should be forgotten from ישראל, as it says: "For it shall not be forgotten from the mouth of his offspring."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with an opposing opinion. רבי שמעון בן יוחי says the תורה will never be forgotten from the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view said that a time will come when people search for the word of ה׳ and fail to find it. רבי שמעון בן יוחי rejects that idea strongly, saying "חס ושלום". His source is a פסוק in דברים that promises the תורה will stay in the mouths of the Jewish people's descendants.

keyTerms.meaning: Heaven forbid; an expression that an idea is unthinkable
From the mouth of his offspring

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a continuation of רבא's discussion about the oven and its airspace. The גמרא has returned to the bigger question that the bread case was illustrating: will the תורה ever be forgotten?
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a direct disagreement with the earlier view. רבי שמעון בן יוחי now has to explain the פסוק that the other side relied on.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
phrases.notes: Now the other side: he disagrees with what we just heard, that the Torah will be forgotten.

phrases.english: Heaven forbid that the Torah should be forgotten from Israel,
as it is said: "For it shall not be forgotten from the mouth of his offspring."

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא רבי שמעון בן יוחי אומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an opposing ברייתא against the earlier view that the תורה will be forgotten. The bread and oven discussion had been illustrating that earlier view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה will never be forgotten from ישראל, based on "כי לא תשכח מפי זרעו".

steps.title: How then do we explain the verse about searching and not finding?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי asks how he can explain the פסוק "ישוטטו לבקש את דבר ה׳ ולא ימצאו", since it seems to say people will not find the word of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the פסוק: "They will roam to seek the word of ה׳, but they will not find it"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי raises the obvious problem with his own view: a פסוק that seems to say the תורה will be lost. This question sets up his explanation, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "אלא מה אני מקיים" means "so how do I make sense of this other פסוק?" The פסוק in עמוס seems to clash with his proof from דברים. He will need to reread it so that the two פסוקים do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: But how do I explain (fulfill) this other פסוק?

phrases.english: But how do I explain
phrases.notes: This is the usual way of asking about a פסוק that seems to go against what he just said.

phrases.english: "They will roam to seek the word of God,
but they will not find it"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי שמעון בן יוחי addresses the פסוק that seems to contradict his statement in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the פסוק in עמוס mean, if the תורה will never be forgotten?

steps.title: Beginning of the answer: what they will not find
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי begins his explanation: the פסוק means "they will not find" something specific. The details continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that they will not find...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי starts to explain the פסוק in עמוס. The sentence continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His approach is to limit what "not finding" means. The פסוק will not mean the תורה disappears completely. It will refer to a narrower kind of loss, which the continuing text will spell out.
steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off here. Do not conclude that רבי שמעון בן יוחי agrees the תורה will be lost. He is about to explain what exactly will not be found.

phrases.english: that they will not find
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question raised in step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק refers to a limited kind of "not finding", not total forgetting. The full answer continues on the next amud.
